experiment_registry.hypothesis: DPO-aligned GPT-2 reduces measured toxicity relative to pretrained GPT-2 and mechanistic interventions identify directions that causally control this behavior.
Probe, MLP, and SVD toxic directions should produce measurable toxicity shifts under generation-time subtraction.
If DPO bypasses toxicity circuits rather than erasing them, un-aligning interventions can recover toxic behavior.

grounding.note: Toxicity scores are treated as calibrated probabilities when classifier backends provide probability-like outputs.
Threshold-sensitive toxicity reporting records calibration version metadata so threshold changes are auditable.
Toxicity is defined as rude, disrespectful, or unreasonable text likely to make people leave a discussion.

paper.core_hypothesis: DPO reduces toxic generations by changing how toxic directions are used in the residual stream rather than by deleting model knowledge; mechanistic probes and vector interventions should expose that pathway.

paper.stop_rule_or_pruning_rationale: Run the paper-specified DPO/PPLM/intervention protocol and bounded similarity-guidance scales [9, 1, 10]; avoid exhaustive sweeps unless --mode full is requested.
paper.title: A Mechanistic Understanding of Alignment Algorithms: A Case Study on DPO and Toxicity

scope.hypothesis: DPO reduces toxic generations by rerouting or suppressing toxicity-relevant representations rather than removing model capability; vector and un-aligning interventions should causally recover or reduce toxicity while preserving the same evaluation interfaces.

out_of_scope.reason: Results related to Llama2 are out of scope for the default runnable route because access to the Llama2 model depends on external permission.
